subject: general
question:
In the question below are given two statements followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements disregarding commonly known facts.

Statements:

All hens are guns.

Some guns are cats.

Conclusions:

I. Some hens are cats.

II. No hen is cat.
solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd4eb37b8d223b53cd03e4e4f196aa3d5cb080c10ab1d3975b71c0261a47d982.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some hens are cats → False (as there is no direct relation given between hen and cat, so no definite conclusion could be drawn)

II. No hen is a cat → False (as there is no direct relation given between hen and cat, so no definite conclusion could be drawn)

Conclusion I and II form a complementary pair.

Hence,** either I or II follows.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Conditions for Either - Or 

 
• Subject and predicate should be the same.
 
• Both individual conclusions should be false.
 
• One conclusion should be positive and one conclusion should be negative.
 
• There should either be one of the following pairs present in the conclusions.

 
• All + Some not
 
• Some + No
